title: Ensuring People-centric Desing in Pedestrian Linkway Planning
what_it_is: Ensuring People-centric Desing in Pedestrian Linkway Planning

sections.label: Overhead bridge lifts stop
sections.summary: After the last train, overhead bridge lifts stop, so the bridge is no longer barrier-free and residents must use stairs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: After 12.35 am, when the last train has gone, the lifts at the overhead bridge stop operating.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Hence, the overhead bridge is no longer a barrier-free facility.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: As the ground level pedestrian crossing has already been removed, residents, particularly seniors with mobility issues, have no choice but to walk up the stairs to cross the road.

sections.label: Barrier-free crossing replaced by bridge
sections.summary: The previous barrier-free pedestrian crossing was replaced by an overhead link bridge whose lifts shut down after the last MRT train.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, the previous barrier-free pedestrian crossing is gone.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: It has been replaced by an overhead link bridge which is barrier-free and only during certain hours of the day – the lifts shut down after the last MRT train has gone.

sections.label: Rejected link bridge proposals
sections.summary: Link bridge proposals connecting private developments and malls to HDB buildings were rejected, including Clementi Mall and 321 Clementi.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, this vision sometimes is more aspiration than reality.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: There have been examples of link bridges proposed to connect private developments, private shopping malls to HDB buildings where the proposals were rejected.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In my own ward of Clementi, this was the case for Clementi Mall, as well as the new "321 Clementi"; in both cases, missed opportunities to improve pedestrian access, missed opportunities to reduce the risk of traffic accidents.

sections.label: Stronger building code incentives
sections.summary: The building code needs stronger incentives, perhaps making such access mandatory for projects in built-up HDB town centres.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Our building code needs stronger incentives, perhaps even making such access mandatory for projects in already built-up HDB town centres.

sections.label: Building Code barrier-free crossings requirement
sections.summary: The Building Code review should require private developers to provide barrier-free overhead crossings to nearby HDB developments or allocate white space.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Likewise, I would propose that the Building Code, at its next review, should require private developers to make provision for barrier-free overhead crossings to nearby HDB developments, either at the time of construction, or by allocating white space for future crossings where the Town Centre is not yet fully mature.

sections.label: More pedestrian connectivity to amenities
sections.summary: More pedestrian connectivity from residential estates to key amenities and transport nodes will be provided, using ground-level crossings and above-ground or underground linkages.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: First, we will provide more pedestrian connectivity from residential estates to key amenities and transport nodes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Some of these connections will be in the form of ground-level direct crossings, because that is the most direct way of getting from point to point and some will be involving above-ground or underground linkages to enhance connectivity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: These are more costly to do than at grade linkways, the above-ground and underground linkages, but we will do so in areas with higher pedestrian volumes, such as in our town and regional centres.

sections.label: Walk2Ride covered linkway extension
sections.summary: LTA's Walk2Ride scheme will extend the covered linkway network to about 200 kilometres of sheltered walkways by 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: LTA has a scheme to do this, called the Walk2Ride scheme, and I am happy to share that they will be extending the covered linkway network under this scheme to about 200 kilometres of sheltered walkways by 2018.

sections.label: Sheltered walkways to hospital
sections.summary: Bus services run from the MRT station to the hospital, and sheltered walkways will be provided for most of the walking stretch.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, to provide better connectivity, we have bus services from the MRT station to the hospital and we are going to make sure that, as far as possible, for most of the stretch when you walk from the MRT station to the hospital, there will be sheltered walkways provided as well.

sections.label: All-day barrier-free overhead bridge access
sections.summary: LTA and SMRT will adopt the suggestion to provide all-day barrier-free access to and from the overhead bridge.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: As Dr Tan Wu Meng mentioned, they have been hard at work with SMRT.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And I am happy to announce that LTA and SMRT will be adopting his suggestion to provide all-day barrier-free access to and from the overhead bridge.

sections.label: Linkway conditions and compulsion legislation
sections.summary: URA will impose linkway land sales conditions where feasible, and legislation is being studied to compel building owners to provide pedestrian links.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Wherever feasible, the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) will impose this as a land sales condition on developers that they have to build underground at-grade or elevated linkways connected to their developments and to enhance the pedestrian experience.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And Dr Tan Wu Meng shared some of his experience in Clementi with difficulties getting some of the existing malls to put in place connections.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are, indeed, studying how legislation needs to be enhanced, potentially, to give us the ability to compel building owners to provide such pedestrian links.

sections.label: Road closures and car-free Sunday
sections.summary: MND and MOT launched more weekend road closures and a car-free Sunday in the civic district on the last Sunday of the month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why we have to make progress towards such a goal and we are trying to sensitise and get people used to such a mindset.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why MND and MOT have launched more road closures over the weekends and we have recently started a car-free Sunday in the civic district on the last Sunday of the month.

sections.label: Building a better walking Singapore
sections.summary: With stakeholder support, Singapore can be built as one of the best cities for walking and active urban mobility.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: With the support of all stakeholders, I am confident we can build an even better Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We can build a Singapore that is not just the greenest and most beautiful city in the world, but, potentially, one of the best cities for walking and for active urban mobility.
